candidates.title: RNA sequencing of antennae and comparative analysis of key gene families in Apis mellifera workers exhibiting drastic differences in propolis yield.
candidates.measured: Apis mellifera foragers from high-propolis vs ordinary colonies (hives of about 3,000-3,500 workers, per methods). Antennal morphology, antennal RNA-seq, qRT-PCR of 58 genes in three olfactory gene families (6 CSPs, 19 OBPs, 34 ORs). Effect: antennae and flagellomeres FL7, FL10 shorter in high-propolis colonies.
candidates.field_claim_paraphrase: Wax economy of hexagonal cells relative to the next-best regular tessellation (honeycomb conjecture).
candidates.relevance_reason: Olfaction and propolis foraging. Nothing on comb geometry, cell shape or wax. The word 'honeycomb' occurs once, in a rearing sentence in the methods.
lexical_false_positives: 'honeycomb' (one rearing sentence in the methods: pupae placed on comb to emerge)
numbers '7' and '10' extracted by the deviation extractor are flagellomere names FL7 and FL10, not quantities

quotes.quote: We compared the antennal morphology and RNA-seq profiles of foragers from high propolis-producing and ordinary colonies of A. mellifera worker bees

candidates.title: Altitude-induced hypoxia suppresses Varroa mite reproduction in Tibetan honey bees.
candidates.measured: Apis mellifera ligustica colonies moved between low and high altitude (554 m to 3,637 m) on the Tibetan Plateau, 2023-2024, plus low-altitude colonies held under hypoxia. Varroa destructor fecundity and offspring development, e.g. no mated adult female mite offspring in n = 178 infested cells at high altitude. Full text only: brood-nest temperature and humidity were logged every 5 min in 3 colonies at each of 2 sites as a confound check. Site means were 34.1-34.2 C and 34.4-34.6 C. Worker brood development was not delayed (about 21 days egg to adult).
candidates.field_claim_paraphrase: Precision (SD) of honeybee brood-nest temperature about a 35 C target across ambient -30 C to +45 C.
candidates.relevance_reason: The abstract does not address thermoregulation: its subject is mite reproduction under hypoxia. The full text has a small side measurement of brood-nest temperature at two very different sites. It reports means only. The SD the field defines is not given in the text, and the 5-min series are in S1/S2 Data, which were not read. This is a lead for the field, not a reading of it.
lexical_false_positives: the query's 'nest temperature' matched only the full text's confound-check section, not the abstract

quotes.quote: highlights a previously unrecognized sensitivity of this mite to reduced oxygen availability
ranging from 34.1 to 34.2 °C in Lhasa and 34.4 to 34.6 °C in Xishuangbanna

stub_verdicts.reason: Oxygen acts on the mite, not on the colony's thermoregulation. BE.collective_thermoregulation lists colony_size, ambient_temperature and food_stores, not oxygen. The full text reports that worker development was not delayed under hypoxia.

candidates.disposition_reason: An abstract-only reading would find nothing for this field. Any use of the brood-nest series needs S1/S2 Data and a full-text reading, which the declared pass ('reads: abstract only') does not cover. That is the owner's decision. Reject the HX4 stub either way.
candidates.reader: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), working in Perplexity Computer

candidates.title: Male bumblebees are capable of providing brood care and impacting nest development in incipient nests.
candidates.measured: Bombus impatiens lab-reared incipient nests: 75 queens in four configurations (queen alone n = 29; +1 male n = 18; +3 males n = 15; +5 males n = 13), colonies at about 24-27 C. FLIR T650sc thermal imaging (stated accuracy +/-1 C) over 28 days. Males incubate brood, nest development improves with males present, and males keep a larger thorax-abdomen temperature differential than queens.
candidates.field_claim_paraphrase: Precision (SD) of honeybee (Apis) cluster brood-nest temperature about 35 C across ambient -30 C to +45 C.
candidates.relevance_reason: Brood incubation in a social bee is on the same subject. But the genus differs (Bombus, not Apis), the measure is individual body-surface temperature, not colony brood-nest precision, and ambient temperature was held constant, so precision across ambient was not tested.
lexical_false_positives: the query's '(Apis OR honeybee)' clause matched only 'honeybee-collected pollen' and 'honeybee wax' in the methods; the study organism is Bombus
'temperature' (HX4) here is heat produced by incubating bees, not an ambient condition

quotes.quote: males maintain a greater heat differential between the thorax and abdomen during incubation, suggesting sex-specific differences in thermal regulation

stub_verdicts.reason: The dependency runs the other way. The temperatures named are produced by the insects (thorax heat), while ambient was held near 27 C. The field's dependency, ambient_temperature, was not varied.

candidates.disposition_reason: Does not bear on the Apis field as defined. Using it as a cross-taxon example (cross_domain_examples) would be the owner's call. It is not evidence for the value.

candidates.title: Crop-adapted arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi in maize: from symbiotic function to field reliability.
candidates.measured: Narrative review (no new data) of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi in maize: diversity, arbuscule-mediated exchange, host genotype, P availability, field reliability. Proposes a six-stage 'Maize-Soil-AMF Fit Framework'. The full text cites a 33P-uptake result for a ZmPT6 transporter mutant but gives no transfer fraction.
candidates.field_claim_paraphrase: Fraction of radiotracer-labelled P mobilised by mycorrhizal hyphae that reaches host roots within 72 h under field-comparable pot conditions. The value 0.85 'represents ectomycorrhizal networks in temperate forest soils'.
candidates.relevance_reason: On the subject of mycorrhizal P exchange and its dependence on soil P availability. But it is a review of AMF in maize, not ECM in temperate forest; there is no radiotracer fraction and no 72 h window. Its own caveat is that colonisation does not establish transfer.

quotes.quote: Root colonization alone does not establish effective nutrient transfer or net crop benefit.
It is a conceptual decision aid, not a validated predictive model.

stub_verdicts.reason: Soil phosphorus availability is named as a condition of AMF benefit, and the field lists soil_phosphorus_availability as a dependency. The direction is condition to entity.

candidates.disposition_reason: Worth a reading-ledger entry once the owner registers the source. An outside reader would decide claim_support; this reading assigns none. It does not state the field's number, and its fungal group (AMF) is outside the value's stated ECM scope.

candidates.title: Ectomycorrhizal fungi in deep soils: current knowledge, functional roles, and future directions.
candidates.measured: Review (no new data) of ectomycorrhizal fungi in deep forest soil horizons: vertical community turnover, methods (long-read metabarcoding, isotopes), and possible roles in carbon translocation, N and P mobilisation, and hydraulic redistribution. There is no P transfer fraction and no 32P/33P tracer result.
candidates.field_claim_paraphrase: Fraction of radiotracer-labelled P reaching host roots within 72 h. The value 0.85 'represents ectomycorrhizal networks in temperate forest soils'.
candidates.relevance_reason: The same fungal group and ecosystem as the value's stated scope, and it names P mobilisation. The language is hedged ('might contribute'), it gives no fraction and no time window, and it states that deep-soil ECM function is under-measured.
lexical_false_positives: 'oxygen', 'water', 'carbon' (HX4) refer to deep-soil gradients and network outputs, not to the P-transfer field

quotes.quote: the mobilization of nitrogen and phosphorus pools that are otherwise poorly accessible
deep-soil ECM fungi remain underrepresented in experimental studies and ecosystem models

stub_verdicts.reason: Nutrient and soil hold: they are conditions the field depends on (soil_phosphorus_availability). Oxygen is named as a driver of ECM community turnover, which is not a declared dependency of this field. Carbon and water are what the network moves (translocation, hydraulic redistribution), so for them the dependency runs the other way.

candidates.disposition_reason: Worth a reading-ledger entry once the owner registers the source. It may also inform the field's measurement_limits (depth). This reading assigns no claim_support and does not state the number.

N content and biomass in soil, microbes, roots and shoots. Drought cut plant biomass by about 40%; warming cut microbial biomass by up to 30%.
candidates.field_claim_paraphrase: Fraction of available soil water extracted per unit root length per day at field capacity.
candidates.relevance_reason: Nitrogen flows and biomass under drought. Root water uptake is not measured; the phrase occurs once, in the discussion.
lexical_false_positives: 'drought' is the treatment; it satisfied the query's OR-clause without any water-uptake measurement

quotes.quote: this advantage disappeared under drought, reducing plant biomass by ~ 40%

stub_verdicts.reason: '~40%' is the reduction in plant biomass under drought, and '~20%' is the increase in microbial biomass in Ext soils. Neither is the field's water-extraction fraction.
Water (drought) and soil hold as conditions the field depends on. Nutrient (N) is the response studied, not a condition of water uptake.
